minutes.headline: Committee approved a 2025 Spain trip, pushed the Turkey Hill window study to FY26, and began FY25 cut planning.
minutes.summary: The committee approved a student trip to Spain, a letter responding to union negotiation requests, and donations. It voted to move the Turkey Hill window engineering request out a year after a long MSBA discussion. It also voted to publicize its intent to move inactive class account funds to a student travel account. The superintendent presented class size and schedule data as groundwork for FY25 cuts.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to move the Turkey Hill window schematics request from this year to the FY2026 priorities, after a long discussion of state building-project reimbursement.
The committee approved a proposed student trip to Spain, with one member saying beforehand they would vote no; the count was not audible.
The committee voted, with two opposed, to announce by Facebook and other free means its intent to move unclaimed class account funds to a new student travel account.
The committee approved its response letter to the union on negotiations, and accepted donations.
The superintendent presented class size and schedule information as groundwork for FY25 budget cuts; no vote was taken on cuts.

why_it_matters: Moving the Turkey Hill window request to FY2026 delays a school building project and its place in the capital plan by a year.
Class account money that sits unclaimed may be redirected to student travel, which could affect families whose students have funds in those accounts or need help with trip costs.
The FY25 class size and schedule discussion is the start of a cut-planning process, so residents may be asked to weigh in on school staffing and course offerings.
watch_next: Next meeting on Dec 20, where the chair's letter to the MSBA executive director is to go on the agenda.
Further outreach to class officers before any final vote on moving class account funds.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the Spain trip, the donations, the LEA letter and the main figures once caption errors are resolved. They differ on the class-account vote count (two opposed vs 4-1), on the Turkey Hill window vote, which ours could not hear, and on the schematics move, which ours records as a vote and the town records only as a decision.
